Environmental Sensor API Client Clients

This package contains clients for various environmental monitoring APIs:

  • coris_client: Coris API client for environmental sensor data
  • conserv_client: Conserv API client for environmental sensor data
  • licor_client: LI-COR API client for environmental sensor data

 95class CorisClient:
 96    """
 97    Client for interacting with the Coris environmental monitoring API.
 98    
 99    This client handles:
100    - Sensor metadata retrieval
101    - Historical sensor data queries
102    - Current sensor readings
103    - Data transformation to standardized schema
104    """
105    
106    def __init__(self, logger: Optional[logging.Logger] = None, home_directory: str = "."):
107        """
108        Initialize the Coris API client.
109        
110        Parameters
111        ----------
112        logger : Optional[logging.Logger]
113            Logger instance for recording API interactions
114        home_directory : str, default="."
115            Base directory for finding .env file
116        """
117        # Read API key from environment variables
118        env_file_path = os.path.join(home_directory, ".env")
119        api_key = None
120        with open(env_file_path) as f:
121            for line in f:
122                if line.startswith("CORIS_API_KEY"):
123                    api_key = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
124                    break
125        
126        # Read CATS User ID from environment variables
127        cats_user_id_str = None
128        with open(env_file_path) as f:
129            for line in f:
130                if line.startswith("CATS_USER_ID"):
131                    cats_user_id_str = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
132                    break
133        
134        if not api_key:
135            raise ValueError(
136                f"CORIS_API_KEY not found in environment or .env file at {env_file_path}. "
137                f"If running from a subdirectory, set home_directory parameter to parent directory (e.g., home_directory='..').")
138        
139        if not cats_user_id_str:
140            raise ValueError(
141                f"CATS_USER_ID not found in environment or .env file at {env_file_path}. "
142                f"If running from a subdirectory, set home_directory parameter to parent directory (e.g., home_directory='..').")
143        
144        self.api_key = api_key
145        self.cats_user_id = cats_user_id_str
146        self.logger = logger or logging.getLogger(__name__)
147        self.base_url = "https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api"
148        
149        # Reading interval in seconds (15 minutes = 900 seconds)
150        # Consistent with Conserv (15-min exports) and LI-COR (downsampled to 15 min)
151        self.reading_spacing_seconds = 900
152    
153    def get_current_utc(self) -> int:
154        """
155        Get the current UTC timestamp in seconds.
156        
157        Returns
158        -------
159        int : Current UTC timestamp
160        """
161        return int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp())

163    def get_sensors(self, out_of_scope: List[str] = None, testing: bool = False, 
164                   testing_sensor_ids: List[int] = None) -> polars.DataFrame:
165        """
166        Get the list of all sensors from the Coris API.
167        
168        Parameters
169        ----------
170        out_of_scope : List[str], optional
171            List of sensor name prefixes to exclude
172        testing : bool, default=False
173            If True, limit to testing sensors only
174        testing_sensor_ids : List[int], optional
175            List of sensor IDs to use when testing mode is enabled
176            
177        Returns
178        -------
179        polars.DataFrame
180            Sensor data with columns: SensorID, DeviceID, SensorName, 
181            DeviceName, SensorType, QueryUTC, source, customer_id
182        """
183        out_of_scope = out_of_scope or []
184        testing_sensor_ids = testing_sensor_ids or []
185        
186        # Build the URL and call the API
187        # self.logger.info("get_sensors")
188        url = f'{self.base_url}/cats/user/?ApiKey={self.api_key}&CatsUserID={self.cats_user_id}'
189        
190        # Log sanitized URL for security
191        self.logger.info(
192            "API call: https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/cats/user/?ApiKey=XXXX&CatsUserID=XXXX"
193        )
194        
195        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
196        response = requests.get(url)
197        
198        # Check for errors
199        if not response.ok:
200            error_msg = f"Error getting sensors: {response.json()}"
201            self.logger.error(error_msg)
202            raise Exception(error_msg)
203        
204        # Process sensor data
205        sensors = polars.DataFrame(response.json()["Sensors"])
206        
207        # Remove out-of-scope sensors
208        for prefix in out_of_scope:
209            sensors = sensors.filter(polars.col("SensorName").str.starts_with(prefix).not_())
210        
211        # If testing, only use selected sensors
212        if testing and len(testing_sensor_ids) > 0:
213            sensors = sensors.filter(polars.col("SensorID").is_in(testing_sensor_ids))
214        
215        # Generate SensorID and DeviceID with coris prefix
216        sensors = sensors.with_columns([
217            polars.concat_str([
218                polars.lit("coris:"),
219                polars.col("SensorID").cast(polars.String)
220            ]).alias("SensorID"),
221            polars.concat_str([
222                polars.lit("coris:"),
223                polars.col("DeviceDevID").cast(polars.String)
224            ]).alias("DeviceID")
225        ])
226        
227        # Add standardized schema columns
228        sensors = sensors.with_columns([
229            polars.lit(current_utc).alias("QueryUTC"),
230            polars.lit("Coris").alias("Source"),
231            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int32).alias("customer_id"),
232        ])
233        
234        return sensors
235    
236    def get_historical_data(self, sensor_id: int, reading_type: str, 
237                          start_utc: int, end_utc: int,
238                          sensor_metadata: polars.DataFrame) -> polars.DataFrame:
239        """
240        Get historical sensor data for a specific sensor and reading type.
241        
242        Parameters
243        ----------
244        sensor_id : int
245            Coris sensor ID
246        reading_type : str
247            Type of reading (e.g., 'SensorReadingF', 'SensorReadingRh')
248        start_utc : int
249            Start time as UTC timestamp
250        end_utc : int
251            End time as UTC timestamp
252        sensor_metadata : polars.DataFrame
253            Sensor metadata to attach to readings
254            
255        Returns
256        -------
257        polars.DataFrame
258            Historical readings with standardized schema
259        """
260        url = "&".join([
261            f'{self.base_url}/sensor/historical/?ApiKey={self.api_key}',
262            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
263            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
264            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
265            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
266            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
267            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
268        ])
269        
270        # Create sanitized URL for logging
271        logurl = "&".join([
272            "https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/sensor/historical/?ApiKey=XXXX",
273            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
274            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
275            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
276            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
277            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
278            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
279        ])
280        
281        query_utc = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp())
282        self.logger.info(f"API call: {logurl}")
283        response = requests.get(url)
284        
285        # Check for errors
286        if not response.ok:
287            error_msg = f"Error getting historical {reading_type} for {sensor_id}: {response.json()}"
288            self.logger.error(error_msg)
289            return polars.DataFrame()  # Return empty DataFrame instead of crashing
290        
291        # Parse CSV response
292        data = polars.read_csv(response.content, has_header=False)
293        data.columns = ["SensorReadingUTC", reading_type]
294        
295        # Add sensor metadata
296        consolidated_sensor_id = f"coris:{sensor_id}"
297        data = data.with_columns(polars.lit(consolidated_sensor_id).alias("SensorID"))
298        sensor_data = sensor_metadata.filter(polars.col("SensorID") == consolidated_sensor_id)
299        
300        if sensor_data.shape[0] > 0:
301            for col in ["SensorName", "DeviceName", "DeviceID", "SensorType"]:
302                if col in sensor_data.columns:
303                    data = data.with_columns(
304                        polars.lit(sensor_data[col].to_list()[0]).alias(col)
305                    )
306        
307        # Add standardized schema columns including QueryUTC and Historical
308        data = data.with_columns([
309            polars.lit("Coris").alias("Source"),
310            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int32).alias("customer_id"),
311            polars.lit(query_utc).alias("QueryUTC"),
312            polars.lit(True).alias("Historical"),
313        ])
314        
315        return data
316    
317    def get_historical_data_bulk(self, acceptable_range: Dict[str, List], 
318                               start_utc: int, end_utc: int,
319                               out_of_scope: List[str] = None,
320                               testing: bool = False,
321                               testing_sensor_ids: List[int] = None) -> List[polars.DataFrame]:
322        """
323        Get historical data for all sensors and reading types.
324        
325        Parameters
326        ----------
327        acceptable_range : Dict[str, List]
328            Dictionary mapping reading types to acceptable ranges
329        start_utc : int
330            Start time as UTC timestamp
331        end_utc : int
332            End time as UTC timestamp
333        out_of_scope : List[str], optional
334            List of sensor name prefixes to exclude
335        testing : bool, default=False
336            If True, limit to first 3 sensors per reading type
337        testing_sensor_ids : List[int], optional
338            List to collect sensor IDs used during testing
339            
340        Returns
341        -------
342        List[polars.DataFrame]
343            List of DataFrames containing historical readings
344        """
345        sensors = self.get_sensors(out_of_scope=out_of_scope, testing=testing, 
346                                 testing_sensor_ids=testing_sensor_ids or [])
347        readings = []
348        
349        for reading_type in acceptable_range:
350            # Get sensor IDs that have this reading type - extract numeric ID from consolidated format
351            sensor_ids = (
352                sensors.filter(polars.col(reading_type).is_nan().not_())["SensorID"]
353                .str.split(":")
354                .list.last()
355                .cast(polars.Int32)
356                .unique()
357                .to_list()
358            )
359            
360            if testing:
361                sensor_ids = sensor_ids[0:3]
362                if testing_sensor_ids is not None:
363                    testing_sensor_ids.extend(sensor_ids)
364            
365            # Query API for each sensor
366            pbar = tqdm.tqdm(total=len(sensor_ids), desc=f"Gather Coris readings: {reading_type}")
367            
368            for sensor_id in sensor_ids:
369                data = self.get_historical_data(
370                    sensor_id=sensor_id,
371                    reading_type=reading_type,
372                    start_utc=start_utc,
373                    end_utc=end_utc,
374                    sensor_metadata=sensors
375                )
376                
377                if not data.is_empty():
378                    readings.append(data)
379                
380                pbar.update(1)
381            
382            pbar.close()
383        
384        return readings

386    def get_current_readings(self, out_of_scope: List[str] = None,
387                           testing: bool = False,
388                           testing_sensor_ids: List[int] = None) -> polars.DataFrame:
389        """
390        Get current sensor readings from the Coris API.
391        
392        Parameters
393        ----------
394        out_of_scope : List[str], optional
395            List of sensor name prefixes to exclude
396        testing : bool, default=False
397            If True, limit to testing sensors only
398        testing_sensor_ids : List[int], optional
399            List of sensor IDs to use when testing mode is enabled
400            
401        Returns
402        -------
403        polars.DataFrame
404            Current sensor readings with standardized schema
405        """
406        sensors = self.get_sensors(
407            out_of_scope=out_of_scope,
408            testing=testing,
409            testing_sensor_ids=testing_sensor_ids
410        )
411        
412        # Add schema columns for compatibility including Historical
413        sensors = sensors.with_columns([
414            polars.lit("Coris").cast(polars.String).alias("Source"),
415            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int32).alias("customer_id"),
416            polars.lit(False).alias("Historical"),
417        ])
418        
419        return sensors

421    def sample_raw_data(self, save_to_samples: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
422        """
423        Generate sample raw API data for testing and exploration.
424        
425        This method fetches raw data from the Coris API and optionally saves it
426        to the samples directory with timestamps. Fetches sensor metadata and 
427        sample historical data from multiple sensors for comprehensive testing.
428        
429        Parameters
430        ----------
431        save_to_samples : bool, default=True
432            Whether to save the raw responses to samples/coris/ directory
433            
434        Returns
435        -------
436        Dict[str, Any]
437            Dictionary containing the raw API responses:
438            {
439                'sensors': raw_sensors_response,
440                'historical_data_samples': [list of raw historical data responses]
441            }
442        """
443        results = {}
444        
445        print("🔍 Fetching raw sensor data...")
446        # Get raw sensors data - make direct API call to get raw response
447        url = f'{self.base_url}/cats/user/?ApiKey={self.api_key}&CatsUserID={self.cats_user_id}'
448        
449        self.logger.info(
450            "API call: https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/cats/user/?ApiKey=XXXX&CatsUserID=XXXX"
451        )
452        
453        response = requests.get(url)
454        
455        if not response.ok:
456            error_msg = f"Error getting sensors: {response.json()}"
457            self.logger.error(error_msg)
458            raise Exception(error_msg)
459        
460        raw_sensors = response.json()
461        results['sensors'] = raw_sensors
462        
463        if save_to_samples:
464            timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
465            filename = f"raw_sensors_response_{timestamp}.json"
466            filepath = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "samples" / "coris" / filename
467            filepath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
468            with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
469                json.dump(raw_sensors, f, indent=2, default=str)
470            print(f"Saved sensors data to: {filepath}")
471        
472        sensors_data = raw_sensors.get('Sensors', [])
473        print(f"✅ Retrieved {len(sensors_data)} sensors")
474        
475        # Try to get sample historical data from multiple sensors
476        historical_data_samples = []
477        max_sensors = 3  # Sample up to 3 sensors
478        sensors_sampled = 0
479        
480        if len(sensors_data) > 0:
481            print(f"🔍 Fetching historical data from up to {max_sensors} sensors...")
482            
483            # Get last 24 hours for quick sample
484            end_time = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
485            start_time = end_time - datetime.timedelta(hours=24)
486            start_utc = int(start_time.timestamp())
487            end_utc = int(end_time.timestamp())
488            
489            # Common reading types to sample
490            reading_types = ['SensorReadingF', 'SensorReadingRh', 'SensorReadingC']
491            
492            for sensor in sensors_data:
493                if sensors_sampled >= max_sensors:
494                    break
495                
496                sensor_id = sensor.get('SensorID')
497                sensor_name = sensor.get('SensorName', 'Unknown Sensor')
498                
499                if not sensor_id:
500                    continue
501                
502                print(f"\n📊 Sensor: {sensor_name} (ID: {sensor_id})")
503                
504                # Try to get data for different reading types
505                for reading_type in reading_types:
506                    # Check if this sensor has this reading type
507                    if reading_type in sensor and sensor.get(reading_type) is not None:
508                        print(f"  🔍 Fetching {reading_type} data...")
509                        
510                        url = "&".join([
511                            f'{self.base_url}/sensor/historical/?ApiKey={self.api_key}',
512                            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
513                            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
514                            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
515                            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
516                            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
517                            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
518                        ])
519                        
520                        logurl = "&".join([
521                            "https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/sensor/historical/?ApiKey=XXXX",
522                            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
523                            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
524                            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
525                            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
526                            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
527                            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
528                        ])
529                        
530                        self.logger.info(f"API call: {logurl}")
531                        response = requests.get(url)
532                        
533                        if response.ok:
534                            # Store raw response text since it's CSV data
535                            raw_historical_data = response.text
536                            
537                            historical_data_samples.append({
538                                'sensor_id': sensor_id,
539                                'sensor_name': sensor_name,
540                                'reading_type': reading_type,
541                                'raw_data': raw_historical_data
542                            })
543                            
544                            if save_to_samples:
545                                timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
546                                filename = f"raw_historical_data_{sensor_id}_{reading_type}_{timestamp}.csv"
547                                filepath = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "samples" / "coris" / filename
548                                filepath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
549                                with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
550                                    f.write(raw_historical_data)
551                                print(f"    💾 Saved to: {filepath}")
552                            
553                            print(f"    ✅ Retrieved {reading_type} data for sensor {sensor_id}")
554                            
555                            # Only sample one reading type per sensor to avoid too much data
556                            break
557                            
558                        else:
559                            print(f"    ⚠️ Could not get {reading_type} data: HTTP {response.status_code}")
560                
561                sensors_sampled += 1
562        
563        results['historical_data_samples'] = historical_data_samples
564        
565        # Print summary
566        print(f"\n📋 Sample Data Summary:")
567        print(f"   • Sensors: {len(sensors_data)} found")
568        print(f"   • Historical data samples: {len(historical_data_samples)} collected from {sensors_sampled} sensors")
569        
570        if historical_data_samples:
571            for i, sample in enumerate(historical_data_samples, 1):
572                print(f"     {i}. {sample['sensor_name']} - {sample['reading_type']} (ID: {sample['sensor_id']})")
573        
574        if save_to_samples:
575            print(f"   • Files saved to: samples/coris/")
576        
577        return results

163    def get_sensors(self, out_of_scope: List[str] = None, testing: bool = False, 
164                   testing_sensor_ids: List[int] = None) -> polars.DataFrame:
165        """
166        Get the list of all sensors from the Coris API.
167        
168        Parameters
169        ----------
170        out_of_scope : List[str], optional
171            List of sensor name prefixes to exclude
172        testing : bool, default=False
173            If True, limit to testing sensors only
174        testing_sensor_ids : List[int], optional
175            List of sensor IDs to use when testing mode is enabled
176            
177        Returns
178        -------
179        polars.DataFrame
180            Sensor data with columns: SensorID, DeviceID, SensorName, 
181            DeviceName, SensorType, QueryUTC, source, customer_id
182        """
183        out_of_scope = out_of_scope or []
184        testing_sensor_ids = testing_sensor_ids or []
185        
186        # Build the URL and call the API
187        # self.logger.info("get_sensors")
188        url = f'{self.base_url}/cats/user/?ApiKey={self.api_key}&CatsUserID={self.cats_user_id}'
189        
190        # Log sanitized URL for security
191        self.logger.info(
192            "API call: https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/cats/user/?ApiKey=XXXX&CatsUserID=XXXX"
193        )
194        
195        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
196        response = requests.get(url)
197        
198        # Check for errors
199        if not response.ok:
200            error_msg = f"Error getting sensors: {response.json()}"
201            self.logger.error(error_msg)
202            raise Exception(error_msg)
203        
204        # Process sensor data
205        sensors = polars.DataFrame(response.json()["Sensors"])
206        
207        # Remove out-of-scope sensors
208        for prefix in out_of_scope:
209            sensors = sensors.filter(polars.col("SensorName").str.starts_with(prefix).not_())
210        
211        # If testing, only use selected sensors
212        if testing and len(testing_sensor_ids) > 0:
213            sensors = sensors.filter(polars.col("SensorID").is_in(testing_sensor_ids))
214        
215        # Generate SensorID and DeviceID with coris prefix
216        sensors = sensors.with_columns([
217            polars.concat_str([
218                polars.lit("coris:"),
219                polars.col("SensorID").cast(polars.String)
220            ]).alias("SensorID"),
221            polars.concat_str([
222                polars.lit("coris:"),
223                polars.col("DeviceDevID").cast(polars.String)
224            ]).alias("DeviceID")
225        ])
226        
227        # Add standardized schema columns
228        sensors = sensors.with_columns([
229            polars.lit(current_utc).alias("QueryUTC"),
230            polars.lit("Coris").alias("Source"),
231            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int32).alias("customer_id"),
232        ])
233        
234        return sensors

def get_historical_data( self, sensor_id: int, reading_type: str, start_utc: int, end_utc: int, sensor_metadata: polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame) -> polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame: 
236    def get_historical_data(self, sensor_id: int, reading_type: str, 
237                          start_utc: int, end_utc: int,
238                          sensor_metadata: polars.DataFrame) -> polars.DataFrame:
239        """
240        Get historical sensor data for a specific sensor and reading type.
241        
242        Parameters
243        ----------
244        sensor_id : int
245            Coris sensor ID
246        reading_type : str
247            Type of reading (e.g., 'SensorReadingF', 'SensorReadingRh')
248        start_utc : int
249            Start time as UTC timestamp
250        end_utc : int
251            End time as UTC timestamp
252        sensor_metadata : polars.DataFrame
253            Sensor metadata to attach to readings
254            
255        Returns
256        -------
257        polars.DataFrame
258            Historical readings with standardized schema
259        """
260        url = "&".join([
261            f'{self.base_url}/sensor/historical/?ApiKey={self.api_key}',
262            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
263            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
264            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
265            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
266            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
267            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
268        ])
269        
270        # Create sanitized URL for logging
271        logurl = "&".join([
272            "https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/sensor/historical/?ApiKey=XXXX",
273            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
274            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
275            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
276            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
277            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
278            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
279        ])
280        
281        query_utc = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp())
282        self.logger.info(f"API call: {logurl}")
283        response = requests.get(url)
284        
285        # Check for errors
286        if not response.ok:
287            error_msg = f"Error getting historical {reading_type} for {sensor_id}: {response.json()}"
288            self.logger.error(error_msg)
289            return polars.DataFrame()  # Return empty DataFrame instead of crashing
290        
291        # Parse CSV response
292        data = polars.read_csv(response.content, has_header=False)
293        data.columns = ["SensorReadingUTC", reading_type]
294        
295        # Add sensor metadata
296        consolidated_sensor_id = f"coris:{sensor_id}"
297        data = data.with_columns(polars.lit(consolidated_sensor_id).alias("SensorID"))
298        sensor_data = sensor_metadata.filter(polars.col("SensorID") == consolidated_sensor_id)
299        
300        if sensor_data.shape[0] > 0:
301            for col in ["SensorName", "DeviceName", "DeviceID", "SensorType"]:
302                if col in sensor_data.columns:
303                    data = data.with_columns(
304                        polars.lit(sensor_data[col].to_list()[0]).alias(col)
305                    )
306        
307        # Add standardized schema columns including QueryUTC and Historical
308        data = data.with_columns([
309            polars.lit("Coris").alias("Source"),
310            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int32).alias("customer_id"),
311            polars.lit(query_utc).alias("QueryUTC"),
312            polars.lit(True).alias("Historical"),
313        ])
314        
315        return data

def get_historical_data_bulk( self, acceptable_range: Dict[str, List], start_utc: int, end_utc: int, out_of_scope: List[str] = None, testing: bool = False, testing_sensor_ids: List[int] = None) -> List[polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame]: 
317    def get_historical_data_bulk(self, acceptable_range: Dict[str, List], 
318                               start_utc: int, end_utc: int,
319                               out_of_scope: List[str] = None,
320                               testing: bool = False,
321                               testing_sensor_ids: List[int] = None) -> List[polars.DataFrame]:
322        """
323        Get historical data for all sensors and reading types.
324        
325        Parameters
326        ----------
327        acceptable_range : Dict[str, List]
328            Dictionary mapping reading types to acceptable ranges
329        start_utc : int
330            Start time as UTC timestamp
331        end_utc : int
332            End time as UTC timestamp
333        out_of_scope : List[str], optional
334            List of sensor name prefixes to exclude
335        testing : bool, default=False
336            If True, limit to first 3 sensors per reading type
337        testing_sensor_ids : List[int], optional
338            List to collect sensor IDs used during testing
339            
340        Returns
341        -------
342        List[polars.DataFrame]
343            List of DataFrames containing historical readings
344        """
345        sensors = self.get_sensors(out_of_scope=out_of_scope, testing=testing, 
346                                 testing_sensor_ids=testing_sensor_ids or [])
347        readings = []
348        
349        for reading_type in acceptable_range:
350            # Get sensor IDs that have this reading type - extract numeric ID from consolidated format
351            sensor_ids = (
352                sensors.filter(polars.col(reading_type).is_nan().not_())["SensorID"]
353                .str.split(":")
354                .list.last()
355                .cast(polars.Int32)
356                .unique()
357                .to_list()
358            )
359            
360            if testing:
361                sensor_ids = sensor_ids[0:3]
362                if testing_sensor_ids is not None:
363                    testing_sensor_ids.extend(sensor_ids)
364            
365            # Query API for each sensor
366            pbar = tqdm.tqdm(total=len(sensor_ids), desc=f"Gather Coris readings: {reading_type}")
367            
368            for sensor_id in sensor_ids:
369                data = self.get_historical_data(
370                    sensor_id=sensor_id,
371                    reading_type=reading_type,
372                    start_utc=start_utc,
373                    end_utc=end_utc,
374                    sensor_metadata=sensors
375                )
376                
377                if not data.is_empty():
378                    readings.append(data)
379                
380                pbar.update(1)
381            
382            pbar.close()
383        
384        return readings

421    def sample_raw_data(self, save_to_samples: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
422        """
423        Generate sample raw API data for testing and exploration.
424        
425        This method fetches raw data from the Coris API and optionally saves it
426        to the samples directory with timestamps. Fetches sensor metadata and 
427        sample historical data from multiple sensors for comprehensive testing.
428        
429        Parameters
430        ----------
431        save_to_samples : bool, default=True
432            Whether to save the raw responses to samples/coris/ directory
433            
434        Returns
435        -------
436        Dict[str, Any]
437            Dictionary containing the raw API responses:
438            {
439                'sensors': raw_sensors_response,
440                'historical_data_samples': [list of raw historical data responses]
441            }
442        """
443        results = {}
444        
445        print("🔍 Fetching raw sensor data...")
446        # Get raw sensors data - make direct API call to get raw response
447        url = f'{self.base_url}/cats/user/?ApiKey={self.api_key}&CatsUserID={self.cats_user_id}'
448        
449        self.logger.info(
450            "API call: https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/cats/user/?ApiKey=XXXX&CatsUserID=XXXX"
451        )
452        
453        response = requests.get(url)
454        
455        if not response.ok:
456            error_msg = f"Error getting sensors: {response.json()}"
457            self.logger.error(error_msg)
458            raise Exception(error_msg)
459        
460        raw_sensors = response.json()
461        results['sensors'] = raw_sensors
462        
463        if save_to_samples:
464            timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
465            filename = f"raw_sensors_response_{timestamp}.json"
466            filepath = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "samples" / "coris" / filename
467            filepath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
468            with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
469                json.dump(raw_sensors, f, indent=2, default=str)
470            print(f"Saved sensors data to: {filepath}")
471        
472        sensors_data = raw_sensors.get('Sensors', [])
473        print(f"✅ Retrieved {len(sensors_data)} sensors")
474        
475        # Try to get sample historical data from multiple sensors
476        historical_data_samples = []
477        max_sensors = 3  # Sample up to 3 sensors
478        sensors_sampled = 0
479        
480        if len(sensors_data) > 0:
481            print(f"🔍 Fetching historical data from up to {max_sensors} sensors...")
482            
483            # Get last 24 hours for quick sample
484            end_time = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
485            start_time = end_time - datetime.timedelta(hours=24)
486            start_utc = int(start_time.timestamp())
487            end_utc = int(end_time.timestamp())
488            
489            # Common reading types to sample
490            reading_types = ['SensorReadingF', 'SensorReadingRh', 'SensorReadingC']
491            
492            for sensor in sensors_data:
493                if sensors_sampled >= max_sensors:
494                    break
495                
496                sensor_id = sensor.get('SensorID')
497                sensor_name = sensor.get('SensorName', 'Unknown Sensor')
498                
499                if not sensor_id:
500                    continue
501                
502                print(f"\n📊 Sensor: {sensor_name} (ID: {sensor_id})")
503                
504                # Try to get data for different reading types
505                for reading_type in reading_types:
506                    # Check if this sensor has this reading type
507                    if reading_type in sensor and sensor.get(reading_type) is not None:
508                        print(f"  🔍 Fetching {reading_type} data...")
509                        
510                        url = "&".join([
511                            f'{self.base_url}/sensor/historical/?ApiKey={self.api_key}',
512                            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
513                            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
514                            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
515                            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
516                            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
517                            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
518                        ])
519                        
520                        logurl = "&".join([
521                            "https://cats.corismonitoring.com/api/sensor/historical/?ApiKey=XXXX",
522                            f"SensorID={sensor_id}",
523                            f"ReadingType={reading_type}",
524                            f"StartUTC={start_utc}",
525                            f"EndUTC={end_utc}",
526                            f"MinReadingSpacing={self.reading_spacing_seconds}",
527                            "RequestedOutputFormat=raw",
528                        ])
529                        
530                        self.logger.info(f"API call: {logurl}")
531                        response = requests.get(url)
532                        
533                        if response.ok:
534                            # Store raw response text since it's CSV data
535                            raw_historical_data = response.text
536                            
537                            historical_data_samples.append({
538                                'sensor_id': sensor_id,
539                                'sensor_name': sensor_name,
540                                'reading_type': reading_type,
541                                'raw_data': raw_historical_data
542                            })
543                            
544                            if save_to_samples:
545                                timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
546                                filename = f"raw_historical_data_{sensor_id}_{reading_type}_{timestamp}.csv"
547                                filepath = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "samples" / "coris" / filename
548                                filepath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
549                                with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
550                                    f.write(raw_historical_data)
551                                print(f"    💾 Saved to: {filepath}")
552                            
553                            print(f"    ✅ Retrieved {reading_type} data for sensor {sensor_id}")
554                            
555                            # Only sample one reading type per sensor to avoid too much data
556                            break
557                            
558                        else:
559                            print(f"    ⚠️ Could not get {reading_type} data: HTTP {response.status_code}")
560                
561                sensors_sampled += 1
562        
563        results['historical_data_samples'] = historical_data_samples
564        
565        # Print summary
566        print(f"\n📋 Sample Data Summary:")
567        print(f"   • Sensors: {len(sensors_data)} found")
568        print(f"   • Historical data samples: {len(historical_data_samples)} collected from {sensors_sampled} sensors")
569        
570        if historical_data_samples:
571            for i, sample in enumerate(historical_data_samples, 1):
572                print(f"     {i}. {sample['sensor_name']} - {sample['reading_type']} (ID: {sample['sensor_id']})")
573        
574        if save_to_samples:
575            print(f"   • Files saved to: samples/coris/")
576        
577        return results

class ConservAPIClient: 
 53class ConservAPIClient:
 54    """
 55    Client for the Conserv API that handles export → status → download workflow.
 56    Supports multiple customer tenants and handles the 7-day window limitation.
 57    """
 58
 59    def __init__(self, logger: Optional[logging.Logger] = None, home_directory: str = "."):
 60        """
 61        Initialize the Conserv API client.
 62
 63        Parameters
 64        ----------
 65        logger : Optional[logging.Logger]
 66            Logger instance for tracking operations
 67        home_directory : str, default="."
 68            Base directory for finding .env file
 69        """
 70        # Read configuration from CONSERV_API_KEYS env var (JSON array)
 71        customers = []
 72        env_file_path = os.path.join(home_directory, ".env")
 73        
 74        # First try to read from .env file
 75        try:
 76            with open(env_file_path) as f:
 77                for line in f:
 78                    line = line.strip()
 79                    if line.startswith("CONSERV_API_KEYS=") and "=" in line:
 80                        _, json_value = line.split("=", 1)
 81                        api_keys_list = json.loads(json_value.strip())
 82                        for entry in api_keys_list:
 83                            customers.append({
 84                                'customer_id': entry['id'],
 85                                'api_key': entry['key']
 86                            })
 87                        break
 88        except FileNotFoundError:
 89            raise ValueError(
 90                    f"No .env file found at {env_file_path}. If running from a subdirectory, set home_directory parameter to parent directory (e.g., home_directory='..')."
 91            )
 92
 93        if not customers:
 94            raise ValueError("No Conserv API keys found in .env file")
 95
 96        self.base_url = "https://api.conserv.io"
 97        self.customers = customers
 98        self.logger = logger or logging.getLogger(__name__)
 99        self.max_window_days = 7  # API limitation
100        self.poll_interval_seconds = 10  # How often to check export status (reduced from 30s)
101        self.max_wait_minutes = 15  # Maximum time to wait for export completion
102        
103        # Note: Conserv exports data in 15-minute increments natively.
104        # This is consistent with Coris (MinReadingSpacing=900) and LI-COR (downsampled to 15 min).
105        
106        if logger:
107            logger.info(f"Initialized Conserv client with {len(customers)} customers")
108
109    def _make_api_request(
110        self, method: str, endpoint: str, api_key: str, **kwargs
111    ) -> requests.Response:
112        """
113        Make a request to the Conserv API with proper headers and error handling.
114        SSL issues are expected so we handle them here.
115
116        Parameters
117        ----------
118        method : str
119            HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
120        endpoint : str
121            API endpoint (without base URL)
122        api_key : str
123            Customer API key
124        **kwargs
125            Additional arguments for requests
126
127        Returns
128        -------
129        requests.Response
130            Response object
131        """
132        url = f"{self.base_url}{endpoint}"
133        headers = {"x-api-key": api_key, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
134
135        # Log the request (without sensitive key)
136        safe_headers = {**headers, "x-api-key": "XXXX"}
137        self.logger.info(f"Conserv API {method} {url} headers={safe_headers}")
138
139        try:
140            # Try the regular request. This is preferred even if we expect it to fail.
141            response = requests.request(
142                method, url, headers=headers, verify=True, **kwargs
143            )
144            response.raise_for_status()
145            return response
146        
147        # SSL verification fails for api.conserv.io, retry without verification.
148        # Suppress verbose logging since this is expected behavior.
149        except requests.exceptions.SSLError as e:
150            urllib3.disable_warnings(urllib3.exceptions.InsecureRequestWarning)
151            
152            try:
153                response = requests.request(
154                    method, url, headers=headers, verify=False, **kwargs
155                )
156                response.raise_for_status()
157                return response
158            
159            except requests.exceptions.RequestException as retry_error:
160                # If the retry also fails, log and re-raise with cleaner error context
161                if isinstance(retry_error, requests.exceptions.HTTPError):
162                    self.logger.error(f"API request failed after SSL fallback: {retry_error.response.status_code} {retry_error.response.reason}")
163                else:
164                    self.logger.error(f"Retry with SSL disabled also failed: {str(retry_error)}")
165                raise retry_error
166            
167            finally:
168                # Always re-enable SSL warnings after the request
169                # Reset to default urllib3 warning behavior
170                import warnings
171                warnings.resetwarnings()
172
173    def launch_export(
174        self, api_key: str, start_time: datetime.datetime, end_time: datetime.datetime
175    ) -> Optional[str]:
176        """
177        Launch a data export for a specific time window with error handling.
178
179        Parameters
180        ----------
181        api_key : str
182            Customer API key
183        start_time : datetime.datetime
184            Start time for export (UTC)
185        end_time : datetime.datetime
186            End time for export (UTC)
187
188        Returns
189        -------
190        Optional[str]
191            Export UUID for polling status, or None if launch failed
192        """
193
194        # Validate window size
195        window_days = (end_time - start_time).days
196        if window_days > self.max_window_days:
197            raise ValueError(
198                f"Export window of {window_days} days exceeds maximum of {self.max_window_days} days"
199            )
200
201        response = self._make_api_request(
202            "POST", 
203            "/v1/sensors/export", 
204            api_key, 
205            json={"start": start_time.isoformat(), "end": end_time.isoformat()}
206        )
207
208        result = response.json()
209
210        uuid = result.get("uuid")
211        if not uuid:
212            raise ValueError(f"No UUID returned from export launch: {result}")
213
214        self.logger.info(f"Conserv export launched: {uuid}")
215        return uuid
216
217    def export_data(
218        self,
219        api_key: str,
220        customer_id: str | int,
221        start_time: datetime.datetime,
222        end_time: datetime.datetime,
223    ) -> Optional[polars.DataFrame]:
224        """
225        Complete export workflow: launch → wait → download for a single customer.
226
227        Parameters
228        ----------
229        api_key : str
230            Customer API key
231        customer_id : str | int
232            Customer ID for data tagging
233        start_time : datetime.datetime
234            Start time for export (UTC)
235        end_time : datetime.datetime
236            End time for export (UTC)
237
238        Returns
239        -------
240        Optional[polars.DataFrame]
241            Sensor data with customer_id added, or None if no data found
242        """
243        
244        self.logger.info(
245            f"Starting export for customer {customer_id}: {start_time} to {end_time}"
246        )
247
248        # Launch export
249        uuid = self.launch_export(api_key, start_time, end_time)
250        if uuid is None:
251            return None
252
253        # Wait for completion - inline wait_for_export_completion
254        wait_start_time = time.time()
255        max_wait_seconds = self.max_wait_minutes * 60
256        query_utc = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp())
257
258        while time.time() - wait_start_time < max_wait_seconds:
259            # Check export status - inline check_export_status
260            response = self._make_api_request(
261                "GET", f"/v1/sensors/export/{uuid}/status", api_key
262            )
263            result = response.json()
264            status = result.get("status")
265            if not status:
266                raise ValueError(f"No status returned for export {uuid}: {result}")
267
268            if status == "completed":
269                export_duration = time.time() - wait_start_time
270                self.logger.info(f"Export {uuid} completed successfully in {export_duration:.1f} seconds")
271                break
272            elif status == "failed":
273                self.logger.error(f"Export {uuid} failed")
274                return None
275            elif status in ("pending", "processing", "queued"):
276                # Don't log individual status checks to reduce noise
277                time.sleep(self.poll_interval_seconds)
278            else:
279                raise ValueError(f"Unknown export status: {status}")
280        else:
281            raise TimeoutError(
282                f"Export {uuid} did not complete within {self.max_wait_minutes} minutes"
283            )
284
285        # Add delay to ensure download URL is ready after export completion
286        time.sleep(5)
287
288        # Get download URL - inline get_download_url
289        response = self._make_api_request(
290            "POST", f"/v1/sensors/export/{uuid}/download", api_key
291        )
292        result = response.json()
293        download_url = result.get("url")
294        if not download_url:
295            raise ValueError(f"No download URL returned for export {uuid}: {result}")
296
297        # Download and parse data - inline download_export_data
298        self.logger.info("Downloading export data from S3")
299        response = requests.get(download_url)
300        response.raise_for_status()
301        csv_content = response.content
302        # Read all columns as strings to avoid schema mismatches during concatenation
303        df = polars.read_csv(io.BytesIO(csv_content), infer_schema=False)
304        self.logger.info(f"Downloaded {df.shape[0]} rows, {df.shape[1]} columns")
305
306        if df.shape[0] == 0:
307            self.logger.info(f"No data found for customer {customer_id}")
308            return None
309
310            # Add customer_id and QueryUTC columns
311        df = df.with_columns(
312            [
313                polars.lit(customer_id).alias("customer_id"),
314                polars.lit(query_utc).alias("QueryUTC"),
315            ]
316        )
317
318        self.logger.info(
319            f"Successfully exported {df.shape[0]} rows for customer {customer_id}"
320        )
321        return df
322
323    def export_data_chunked(
324        self,
325        api_key: str,
326        customer_id: str | int,
327        start_time: datetime.datetime,
328        end_time: datetime.datetime,
329    ) -> List[polars.DataFrame]:
330        """
331        Export data in chunks to handle the 7-day window limitation.
332
333        Parameters
334        ----------
335        api_key : str
336            Customer API key
337        customer_id : str | int
338            Customer ID for data tagging
339        start_time : datetime.datetime
340            Start time for export (UTC)
341        end_time : datetime.datetime
342            End time for export (UTC)
343
344        Returns
345        -------
346        List[polars.DataFrame]
347            List of DataFrames, one per chunk
348        """
349        chunks = []
350        current_start = start_time
351
352        while current_start < end_time:
353            # Calculate chunk end (max 7 days)
354            chunk_end = min(
355                current_start + datetime.timedelta(days=self.max_window_days), end_time
356            )
357
358            self.logger.info(
359                f"Exporting chunk for customer {customer_id}: {current_start} to {chunk_end}"
360            )
361
362            # Export this chunk
363            chunk_data = self.export_data(
364                api_key, customer_id, current_start, chunk_end
365            )
366
367            if chunk_data is not None:
368                chunks.append(chunk_data)
369
370            # Move to next chunk
371            current_start = chunk_end
372
373        return chunks

375    def get_current_data(self, hours_back: int = 6, test: bool = False) -> Optional[polars.DataFrame]:
376        """

395    def get_current_readings(self, test: bool = False) -> Optional[polars.DataFrame]:
396        """
397        Get current readings from all customers (or just the first customer if test=True) for the last 30 minutes.
398        
399        Parameters
400        ----------
401        test : bool, default=False
402            If True, only use the first customer for testing
403            
404        Returns
405        -------
406        Optional[polars.DataFrame]
407            Current sensor data in standardized format from all customers, or None if no data
408        """
409        if self.logger:
410            self.logger.info("Fetching current readings for last 30 minutes")
411        
412        # Filter customers based on test mode
413        customers_to_process = self.customers
414        if test:
415            customers_to_process = self.customers[:1]  # Only first customer
416            if self.logger:
417                self.logger.info(f"Running in test mode - only processing first customer: {customers_to_process[0]['customer_id']}")
418        
419        all_customer_data = []
420        
421        # Process each customer with progress bar
422        pbar = tqdm.tqdm(total=len(customers_to_process), desc="Gathering Conserv current readings")
423        for customer in customers_to_process:
424            try:
425                if self.logger:
426                    self.logger.info(f"Fetching current data for customer {customer['customer_id']}")
427                
428                # Calculate time range (last 30 minutes)
429                end_time = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
430                start_time = end_time - datetime.timedelta(minutes=30)
431                
432                # Use export_data to get recent data
433                customer_data = self.export_data(
434                    api_key=customer['api_key'],
435                    customer_id=customer['customer_id'],
436                    start_time=start_time,
437                    end_time=end_time
438                )
439                
440                if customer_data is not None and len(customer_data) > 0:
441                    all_customer_data.append(customer_data)
442                    
443                    if self.logger:
444                        self.logger.info(f"Retrieved {len(customer_data)} current records for customer {customer['customer_id']}")
445                else:
446                    if self.logger:
447                        self.logger.info(f"No current data available for customer {customer['customer_id']}")
448                        
449            except Exception as e:
450                if self.logger:
451                    self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch current data for customer {customer['customer_id']}: {e}")
452                # Continue with other customers
453                continue
454            finally:
455                pbar.update(1)
456        
457        pbar.close()
458        
459        # Combine all customer data
460        if all_customer_data:
461            combined_data = polars.concat(all_customer_data, how="vertical")
462            
463            # Filter to only the last reading per sensor name/serial/customer combination
464            # Take the last (most recent) reading for each sensor (assuming chronological order from API)
465            combined_data = (
466                combined_data
467                .group_by(["customer_id", "Sensor Serial", "Sensor Name"])
468                .last()
469            )
470            
471            if self.logger:
472                self.logger.info(f"Filtered to {len(combined_data)} most recent readings per sensor")
473            
474            # Add Historical=False for current readings and transform to standardized schema
475            combined_data = combined_data.with_columns(polars.lit(False).alias("Historical"))
476            combined_data = self.transform_to_standardized_schema(combined_data)
477            
478            if self.logger:
479                self.logger.info(f"Successfully combined current readings from {len(all_customer_data)} customers: {len(combined_data)} total records")
480            
481            return combined_data
482        else:
483            if self.logger:
484                self.logger.warning("No current readings retrieved from any customer")
485            return None

515        )
516        end_time = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(end_utc, tz=datetime.timezone.utc)

518        all_customer_data = []
519        
520        # Filter customers based on test mode

522        if test:
523            customers_to_process = self.customers[:1]  # Only first customer
524            if self.logger:
525                self.logger.info(f"Running in test mode - only processing first customer: {customers_to_process[0]['customer_id']}")
526
527        # Process each customer with progress bar

529        for customer in customers_to_process:
530            try:
531                if self.logger:
532                    self.logger.info(
533                        f"Fetching data for customer {customer['customer_id']}"
534                    )
535
536                # Use chunked export for reliable data retrieval
537                customer_data_chunks = self.export_data_chunked(
538                    api_key=customer['api_key'],
539                    customer_id=customer['customer_id'],
540                    start_time=start_time,
541                    end_time=end_time,
542                )
543
544                if customer_data_chunks:
545                    # Combine all chunks for this customer
546                    customer_data = polars.concat(customer_data_chunks, how="diagonal")
547
548                    all_customer_data.append(customer_data)
549
550                    if self.logger:
551                        self.logger.info(
552                            f"Successfully fetched {customer_data.shape[0]} records for customer {customer['customer_id']}"

559
560            except Exception as e:

564                    )
565                # Continue with other customers
566                continue
567            finally:
568                pbar.update(1)
569
570        pbar.close()
571
572        # Combine all customer data
573        if all_customer_data:
574            combined_data = polars.concat(all_customer_data, how="vertical")            
575
576            # Add Historical column and transform to standardized schema for this customer
577            combined_data = combined_data.with_columns(polars.lit(True).alias("Historical"))
578            combined_data = self.transform_to_standardized_schema(combined_data)
579            
580            if self.logger:
581                self.logger.info(
582                    f"Successfully combined data from {len(all_customer_data)} customers: {combined_data.shape[0]} total records"
583                )
584            return combined_data
585        else:

590    def transform_to_standardized_schema(
591        self, df: polars.DataFrame
592    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
593        """
594        Transform Conserv API data to standardized schema.
595
596        Parameters
597        ----------
598        df : polars.DataFrame
599            Raw Conserv data with columns: Sensor Name, Time, Temperature (°C), Humidity (%), customer_id, source
600
601        Returns
602        -------
603        polars.DataFrame
604            Data transformed to match standardized schema
605        """
606        if self.logger:
607            self.logger.info("Transforming Conserv data to standardized schema")
608
609        # Create a copy to avoid modifying the original
610        df = df.clone()
611
612        # ============ COLUMN TRANSFORMATIONS ============
613
614        # source - rename existing lowercase column to uppercase
615        if "source" in df.columns:
616            df = df.rename({"source": "Source"})
617        else:
618            df = df.with_columns(polars.lit("Conserv").alias("Source"))
619
620        # SensorReadingF - handle potential encoding issues in column names
621        temp_col = None
622        humidity_col = None
623        
624        for col in df.columns:
625            if "Temperature" in col and ("°C" in col or "Â°C" in col):
626                temp_col = col
627            elif "Humidity" in col and "%" in col:
628                humidity_col = col
629        
630        if temp_col is None:
631            raise ValueError(f"Temperature column not found. Available columns: {df.columns}")
632        if humidity_col is None:
633            raise ValueError(f"Humidity column not found. Available columns: {df.columns}")
634        
635        df = df.with_columns(
636            ((polars.col(temp_col).cast(polars.Float32) * 9 / 5) + 32).alias("SensorReadingF")
637        )
638
639        # SensorReadingRh
640        df = df.rename({humidity_col: "SensorReadingRh"})
641        df = df.with_columns(polars.col("SensorReadingRh").cast(polars.Float32))
642
643        # SensorReadingUTC - handle ISO format like "2025-11-15T18:51:01.729Z"
644        df = df.with_columns(
645            polars.col("Time")
646            .str.replace("Z$", "")  # Remove trailing Z if present
647            .str.strptime(polars.Datetime, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%.f")
648            .dt.timestamp("ms")
649            .floordiv(1000)  # Convert milliseconds to seconds
650            .alias("SensorReadingUTC")
651        )
652
653        # DeviceID
654        df = df.with_columns([
655            polars.concat_str([
656                polars.lit("conserv:"),
657                polars.col("customer_id").cast(polars.String),
658                polars.lit(":"),
659                polars.col("Sensor Serial")
660            ]).alias("DeviceId"),
661            polars.col("Sensor Name").alias("DeviceName"),
662        ])
663
664        # DeviceName
665        df = df.with_columns(
666            df["Sensor Name"].alias("DeviceName")
667        )
668
669        # The data comes in already in device oriented format. We need to transform to sensor oriented format.
670        # Transform each row into two rows: one for Temperature sensor and one for RH sensor
671        
672        # Create Temperature sensor rows
673        temp_rows = df.select([
674            polars.col("Historical"),
675            polars.col("SensorReadingUTC"),
676            polars.col("Source"),
677            polars.col("DeviceId").alias("DeviceID"),
678            polars.col("DeviceName"),
679            polars.concat_str([
680                polars.col("DeviceId"),
681                polars.lit(":Temperature")
682            ]).alias("SensorID"),
683            polars.concat_str([
684                polars.col("DeviceId"),
685                polars.lit(":Temperature")
686            ]).alias("SensorName"),
687            polars.lit("Temperature").alias("SensorType"),
688            polars.col("SensorReadingF"),
689            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Float32).alias("SensorReadingRh"),
690            #polars.col("customer_id"),
691            polars.col("QueryUTC")
692        ])
693        
694        # Create RH sensor rows
695        rh_rows = df.select([
696            polars.col("Historical"),
697            polars.col("SensorReadingUTC"),
698            polars.col("Source"),
699            polars.col("DeviceId").alias("DeviceID"),
700            polars.col("DeviceName"),
701            polars.concat_str([
702                polars.col("DeviceId"),
703                polars.lit(":RH")
704            ]).alias("SensorID"),
705            polars.concat_str([
706                polars.col("DeviceId"),
707                polars.lit(":RH")
708            ]).alias("SensorName"),
709            polars.lit("RH").alias("SensorType"),
710            polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Float32).alias("SensorReadingF"),
711            polars.col("SensorReadingRh"),
712            #polars.col("customer_id"),
713            polars.col("QueryUTC")
714        ])
715        
716        # Combine temperature and RH rows
717        df = polars.concat([temp_rows, rh_rows], how="vertical")
718
719        if self.logger:
720            self.logger.info(f"Conserv transformation complete: {df.shape[0]} records (doubled from device to sensor format)")
721
722        return df
723

773        else:

Client for the Conserv API that handles export → status → download workflow. Supports multiple customer tenants and handles the 7-day window limitation.

ConservAPIClient(logger: Optional[logging.Logger] = None, home_directory: str = '.') 
 59    def __init__(self, logger: Optional[logging.Logger] = None, home_directory: str = "."):
 60        """
 61        Initialize the Conserv API client.
 62
 63        Parameters
 64        ----------
 65        logger : Optional[logging.Logger]
 66            Logger instance for tracking operations
 67        home_directory : str, default="."
 68            Base directory for finding .env file
 69        """
 70        # Read configuration from CONSERV_API_KEYS env var (JSON array)
 71        customers = []
 72        env_file_path = os.path.join(home_directory, ".env")
 73        
 74        # First try to read from .env file
 75        try:
 76            with open(env_file_path) as f:
 77                for line in f:
 78                    line = line.strip()
 79                    if line.startswith("CONSERV_API_KEYS=") and "=" in line:
 80                        _, json_value = line.split("=", 1)
 81                        api_keys_list = json.loads(json_value.strip())
 82                        for entry in api_keys_list:
 83                            customers.append({
 84                                'customer_id': entry['id'],
 85                                'api_key': entry['key']
 86                            })
 87                        break
 88        except FileNotFoundError:
 89            raise ValueError(
 90                    f"No .env file found at {env_file_path}. If running from a subdirectory, set home_directory parameter to parent directory (e.g., home_directory='..')."
 91            )
 92
 93        if not customers:
 94            raise ValueError("No Conserv API keys found in .env file")
 95
 96        self.base_url = "https://api.conserv.io"
 97        self.customers = customers
 98        self.logger = logger or logging.getLogger(__name__)
 99        self.max_window_days = 7  # API limitation
100        self.poll_interval_seconds = 10  # How often to check export status (reduced from 30s)
101        self.max_wait_minutes = 15  # Maximum time to wait for export completion
102        
103        # Note: Conserv exports data in 15-minute increments natively.
104        # This is consistent with Coris (MinReadingSpacing=900) and LI-COR (downsampled to 15 min).
105        
106        if logger:
107            logger.info(f"Initialized Conserv client with {len(customers)} customers")

def launch_export( self, api_key: str, start_time: datetime.datetime, end_time: datetime.datetime) -> Optional[str]: 
173    def launch_export(
174        self, api_key: str, start_time: datetime.datetime, end_time: datetime.datetime
175    ) -> Optional[str]:
176        """
177        Launch a data export for a specific time window with error handling.
178
179        Parameters
180        ----------
181        api_key : str
182            Customer API key
183        start_time : datetime.datetime
184            Start time for export (UTC)
185        end_time : datetime.datetime
186            End time for export (UTC)
187
188        Returns
189        -------
190        Optional[str]
191            Export UUID for polling status, or None if launch failed
192        """
193
194        # Validate window size
195        window_days = (end_time - start_time).days
196        if window_days > self.max_window_days:
197            raise ValueError(
198                f"Export window of {window_days} days exceeds maximum of {self.max_window_days} days"
199            )
200
201        response = self._make_api_request(
202            "POST", 
203            "/v1/sensors/export", 
204            api_key, 
205            json={"start": start_time.isoformat(), "end": end_time.isoformat()}
206        )
207
208        result = response.json()
209
210        uuid = result.get("uuid")
211        if not uuid:
212            raise ValueError(f"No UUID returned from export launch: {result}")
213
214        self.logger.info(f"Conserv export launched: {uuid}")
215        return uuid

def export_data( self, api_key: str, customer_id: str | int, start_time: datetime.datetime, end_time: datetime.datetime) -> Optional[polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame]: 
217    def export_data(
218        self,
219        api_key: str,
220        customer_id: str | int,
221        start_time: datetime.datetime,
222        end_time: datetime.datetime,
223    ) -> Optional[polars.DataFrame]:
224        """
225        Complete export workflow: launch → wait → download for a single customer.
226
227        Parameters
228        ----------
229        api_key : str
230            Customer API key
231        customer_id : str | int
232            Customer ID for data tagging
233        start_time : datetime.datetime
234            Start time for export (UTC)
235        end_time : datetime.datetime
236            End time for export (UTC)
237
238        Returns
239        -------
240        Optional[polars.DataFrame]
241            Sensor data with customer_id added, or None if no data found
242        """
243        
244        self.logger.info(
245            f"Starting export for customer {customer_id}: {start_time} to {end_time}"
246        )
247
248        # Launch export
249        uuid = self.launch_export(api_key, start_time, end_time)
250        if uuid is None:
251            return None
252
253        # Wait for completion - inline wait_for_export_completion
254        wait_start_time = time.time()
255        max_wait_seconds = self.max_wait_minutes * 60
256        query_utc = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp())
257
258        while time.time() - wait_start_time < max_wait_seconds:
259            # Check export status - inline check_export_status
260            response = self._make_api_request(
261                "GET", f"/v1/sensors/export/{uuid}/status", api_key
262            )
263            result = response.json()
264            status = result.get("status")
265            if not status:
266                raise ValueError(f"No status returned for export {uuid}: {result}")
267
268            if status == "completed":
269                export_duration = time.time() - wait_start_time
270                self.logger.info(f"Export {uuid} completed successfully in {export_duration:.1f} seconds")
271                break
272            elif status == "failed":
273                self.logger.error(f"Export {uuid} failed")
274                return None
275            elif status in ("pending", "processing", "queued"):
276                # Don't log individual status checks to reduce noise
277                time.sleep(self.poll_interval_seconds)
278            else:
279                raise ValueError(f"Unknown export status: {status}")
280        else:
281            raise TimeoutError(
282                f"Export {uuid} did not complete within {self.max_wait_minutes} minutes"
283            )
284
285        # Add delay to ensure download URL is ready after export completion
286        time.sleep(5)
287
288        # Get download URL - inline get_download_url
289        response = self._make_api_request(
290            "POST", f"/v1/sensors/export/{uuid}/download", api_key
291        )
292        result = response.json()
293        download_url = result.get("url")
294        if not download_url:
295            raise ValueError(f"No download URL returned for export {uuid}: {result}")
296
297        # Download and parse data - inline download_export_data
298        self.logger.info("Downloading export data from S3")
299        response = requests.get(download_url)
300        response.raise_for_status()
301        csv_content = response.content
302        # Read all columns as strings to avoid schema mismatches during concatenation
303        df = polars.read_csv(io.BytesIO(csv_content), infer_schema=False)
304        self.logger.info(f"Downloaded {df.shape[0]} rows, {df.shape[1]} columns")
305
306        if df.shape[0] == 0:
307            self.logger.info(f"No data found for customer {customer_id}")
308            return None
309
310            # Add customer_id and QueryUTC columns
311        df = df.with_columns(
312            [
313                polars.lit(customer_id).alias("customer_id"),
314                polars.lit(query_utc).alias("QueryUTC"),
315            ]
316        )
317
318        self.logger.info(
319            f"Successfully exported {df.shape[0]} rows for customer {customer_id}"
320        )
321        return df

def export_data_chunked( self, api_key: str, customer_id: str | int, start_time: datetime.datetime, end_time: datetime.datetime) -> List[polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame]: 
323    def export_data_chunked(
324        self,
325        api_key: str,
326        customer_id: str | int,
327        start_time: datetime.datetime,
328        end_time: datetime.datetime,
329    ) -> List[polars.DataFrame]:
330        """
331        Export data in chunks to handle the 7-day window limitation.
332
333        Parameters
334        ----------
335        api_key : str
336            Customer API key
337        customer_id : str | int
338            Customer ID for data tagging
339        start_time : datetime.datetime
340            Start time for export (UTC)
341        end_time : datetime.datetime
342            End time for export (UTC)
343
344        Returns
345        -------
346        List[polars.DataFrame]
347            List of DataFrames, one per chunk
348        """
349        chunks = []
350        current_start = start_time
351
352        while current_start < end_time:
353            # Calculate chunk end (max 7 days)
354            chunk_end = min(
355                current_start + datetime.timedelta(days=self.max_window_days), end_time
356            )
357
358            self.logger.info(
359                f"Exporting chunk for customer {customer_id}: {current_start} to {chunk_end}"
360            )
361
362            # Export this chunk
363            chunk_data = self.export_data(
364                api_key, customer_id, current_start, chunk_end
365            )
366
367            if chunk_data is not None:
368                chunks.append(chunk_data)
369
370            # Move to next chunk
371            current_start = chunk_end
372
373        return chunks

def get_current_readings(self, test: bool = False) -> Optional[polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame]: 
395    def get_current_readings(self, test: bool = False) -> Optional[polars.DataFrame]:
396        """
397        Get current readings from all customers (or just the first customer if test=True) for the last 30 minutes.
398        
399        Parameters
400        ----------
401        test : bool, default=False
402            If True, only use the first customer for testing
403            
404        Returns
405        -------
406        Optional[polars.DataFrame]
407            Current sensor data in standardized format from all customers, or None if no data
408        """
409        if self.logger:
410            self.logger.info("Fetching current readings for last 30 minutes")
411        
412        # Filter customers based on test mode
413        customers_to_process = self.customers
414        if test:
415            customers_to_process = self.customers[:1]  # Only first customer
416            if self.logger:
417                self.logger.info(f"Running in test mode - only processing first customer: {customers_to_process[0]['customer_id']}")
418        
419        all_customer_data = []
420        
421        # Process each customer with progress bar
422        pbar = tqdm.tqdm(total=len(customers_to_process), desc="Gathering Conserv current readings")
423        for customer in customers_to_process:
424            try:
425                if self.logger:
426                    self.logger.info(f"Fetching current data for customer {customer['customer_id']}")
427                
428                # Calculate time range (last 30 minutes)
429                end_time = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
430                start_time = end_time - datetime.timedelta(minutes=30)
431                
432                # Use export_data to get recent data
433                customer_data = self.export_data(
434                    api_key=customer['api_key'],
435                    customer_id=customer['customer_id'],
436                    start_time=start_time,
437                    end_time=end_time
438                )
439                
440                if customer_data is not None and len(customer_data) > 0:
441                    all_customer_data.append(customer_data)
442                    
443                    if self.logger:
444                        self.logger.info(f"Retrieved {len(customer_data)} current records for customer {customer['customer_id']}")
445                else:
446                    if self.logger:
447                        self.logger.info(f"No current data available for customer {customer['customer_id']}")
448                        
449            except Exception as e:
450                if self.logger:
451                    self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch current data for customer {customer['customer_id']}: {e}")
452                # Continue with other customers
453                continue
454            finally:
455                pbar.update(1)
456        
457        pbar.close()
458        
459        # Combine all customer data
460        if all_customer_data:
461            combined_data = polars.concat(all_customer_data, how="vertical")
462            
463            # Filter to only the last reading per sensor name/serial/customer combination
464            # Take the last (most recent) reading for each sensor (assuming chronological order from API)
465            combined_data = (
466                combined_data
467                .group_by(["customer_id", "Sensor Serial", "Sensor Name"])
468                .last()
469            )
470            
471            if self.logger:
472                self.logger.info(f"Filtered to {len(combined_data)} most recent readings per sensor")
473            
474            # Add Historical=False for current readings and transform to standardized schema
475            combined_data = combined_data.with_columns(polars.lit(False).alias("Historical"))
476            combined_data = self.transform_to_standardized_schema(combined_data)
477            
478            if self.logger:
479                self.logger.info(f"Successfully combined current readings from {len(all_customer_data)} customers: {len(combined_data)} total records")
480            
481            return combined_data
482        else:
483            if self.logger:
484                self.logger.warning("No current readings retrieved from any customer")
485            return None
